To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

fluorescence polarization can be used to detect penicilloylated proteins in normal serum, and that this method can be used to quantitate penicillin antibodies in normal and immunized human and rabbit sera, as well as in gamma globulin solutions.

the antipenicillin antibodies in human and rabbit sera can be detected in the presence of serum albumin and other non-specific serum factors by means of the fluorescence polarization technique, and that the sensitivity is roughly 0.2 µg of antibody per ml.

(1) antibodies prepared in the rabbit against the hapten, penicilloylgamma globulin, are apparently directed exclusively against this hapten; (2) these antibodies can be absorbed by fluorescein-penicilloyl hapters; and (3) fluorescence polarization can be employed for the detection of these penicilloylated hapters and for the determination of the concentrations of the penicillocy antibodies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new technique, fluorescence polarization, for the detection and measurement of antibodies.
a study of penicillin antibodies by fluorescence polarization and immuno-diffusion.
the use of fluorescence polarization as an assay for the presence of antibodies to penicillin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fluorescence polarization method, as applied to the present study, is not a suitable means of detecting penicilloylspecific antibodies.
fluorescence polarization is an effective method for the quantitative detection of antipenicillocylic antibodies, but that the method is not yet sufficiently refined to be of clinical utility.
the antipenicillin antibodies of both rabbit and man can be demonstrated by fluorescence polarization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fluorescence polarization is a sensitive and convenient method of detecting penicilloylspecific antibodies in human sera.
fluorescence polarization, when used in conjunction with the proper hapten, may be a useful technique for the detection and estimation of antibodies directed against penicilloyls or penicillins.
fluorescence polarization is a very sensitive method for the study of antipeniciloyl antibodies, but that the non-specific binding of the peniciloyl haptens by the serum proteins is a major problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fluorescence polarization can provide a rapid and simple means of screening large numbers of sera, or even plasma, for antibodies to penicillic acid or penicilloylated compounds.
fluorescence polarization can be employed to measure the concentration of antipenicil-loyl antibodies with a sensitivity comparable to that of radioimmunoassays, without the need for radioisotopes.
fluorescence polarization can be used as a sensitive and specific method for detecting penicilloylated proteins.
